shouldFix.title: The carrier repair leaves policyProvenance declared type string while its new whenPresent block and its own fixture require an object, inverting accept and refuse
evidence: The member declares a scalar type. consentRecordsScopeShape.members[policyProvenance] carries "type": "string" with nullable true.

The same member now declares a composite shape for exactly the non-null case. whenPresent is {"kind":"source-identity","type":"object","nullable":false,"closedMembers":["authority","artifactPath","selector","digest"],"digestEncoding":"64-hex-lowercase-sha256","stringsNonEmptyBounded":true,"maxStringBytes":512,"extrasRejected":true}. Since the member is null under invocation-time-naming and present under pre-existing-policy, there is no third state in which the declared string type could apply.

The artifact's own fixture inverts the declared type. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE parentRecords[1] supplies policyProvenance as a real JSON object with the four members and expects accept-shape; parentRecords[4] supplies the JSON string "not-an-object" under pre-existing-policy and expects refuse. So the fixture requires that a string value be refused, while the member declares the type of a legal value to be string.

The artifact has an established convention for this exact case in the same members array, and policyProvenance is the only member that departs from it. byteCap declares "object-or-null" and targetIdentity declares "discriminated-object-or-null"; both carry composite shapes alongside. policyProvenance keeps "string".

This was introduced by the repair under review. In predecessor v10 the member was "type":"string" with closedValuesWhenPresent: true, which is at least type-consistent with a scalar. v11 replaced the boolean with a closed object shape, which is one of the two options Codex offered, and did not update the type declaration that the chosen option required.

Codex's frozen requiredRepair anticipated the choice: 'Replace closedValuesWhenPresent: true with an actual finite value list if the provenance vocabulary is closed, or with an explicit non-empty/bounded source-identity type or closed object shape if it is not.' The first branch would have kept type string; the second, which v11 took, does not.
shouldFix.impact: The pre-existing-policy branch is unsatisfiable as literally written: a validator honoring "type":"string" rejects the object that whenPresent and FC-CARRIER-SHAPE parentRecords[1] mandate, and a validator honoring whenPresent rejects any string. The disagreement is in the fail-open direction for the case the repair exists to close, because a checker that stops at the declared type accepts the bare string "not-an-object" that parentRecords[4] requires be refused, and with it any unstructured prose provenance carrying no digest. That is precisely the malformed-value constraint Codex said implementations could not resolve.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Change /authorizationRecord/consentRecordsScopeShape/members/[10].type from "string" to "object-or-null", matching the convention byteCap already uses in the same members array, so that the declared type, the whenPresent block and FC-CARRIER-SHAPE agree. If instead the intent is a scalar, take Codex's other branch and replace whenPresent with a finite value list, but the present fixture forecloses that reading.

shouldFix.title: The carrier repair is applied only to the serialized scope; the authorization record's own policyProvenance stays unstructured prose, so legal record values have no destination under the mapping's stated totality rule
evidence: The record member received no shape. closedMembers[14] is in full {"name":"policyProvenance","required":true,"nullable":true,"semantics":"For pre-existing-policy: the exact policy source identity. Null with reason for invocation-time-naming."}. There is no closed member set, no digest encoding, no extrasRejected, and no bound. Its legal values are any string.
Its serialized destination now demands a closed four-member digest-bearing object, per whenPresent as quoted in CLAUDE-HEA11-S1.

The artifact's own mapping rule makes that gap a defect in terms. doctorV4FieldMapping.rule reads: 'Total over the 19 authorizationRecord closed members AND over every legal value of those members. Key-set equality is necessary and not sufficient. A legal variant with no destination is a defect. An authorizationRecord member with no destination is a defect in this contract, not a licence to drop it.' A record whose policyProvenance is the legal value 'our internal security policy' is a legal variant with no destination, because that value cannot become a four-member object carrying a 64-hex digest.

The mapping entry does not carry the structure either. destinations.policyProvenance reads only 'consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance when carrier is pre-existing-policy', so nothing in the mapping layer communicates the new closed shape back to the record side.

The convention exists at the record layer and is applied to a sibling member. closedMembers productAdmissionRefs carries closedItemShape [authority, artifactPath, selector, digest, standing, scope], which is the same source-identity idiom v11 just introduced for serialized policyProvenance. So the record layer is capable of carrying this shape and simply was not updated.

This is the recurrence of the pattern I raised as CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 against v9, at a different member. There the record layer's actionSubtype conditionals lagged the serialized layer; v11 repaired that, then introduced the mirror lag on policyProvenance.
shouldFix.impact: The authorization record is the artifact on which GRANTED or DENIED is resolved, and it is the weaker of the two layers for policy-carried consent. A record can satisfy the record schema with an unverifiable prose provenance and no digest, which is exactly the failure mode the contract polices elsewhere: closedMembers productAdmissionRefs states that 'a moved digest or unverifiable prose-only ref DENIES', and FC-STALE-CONTRACT-REF tests it. Under pre-existing-policy consent there is now no equivalent record-layer guarantee. FC-ROUND-TRIP cannot recover it either, since it tests that serialization does not drop or relabel members and there is no structured record-side value to preserve.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Give /authorizationRecord/closedMembers/[14] the same closed source-identity shape the serialized member now carries, in the idiom already used by productAdmissionRefs: a closedItemShape or closedMembers of [authority, artifactPath, selector, digest] with the digest encoding stated, so that every legal record value has a destination and doctorV4FieldMapping.rule's totality claim holds. Extend destinations.policyProvenance to name that shape, and add a record-layer row to FC-CARRIER-SHAPE so the record branch is exercised and not only the serialized one.

shouldFix.title: v11 overwrites the v10 repair record for Codex HAE9-CX-01 rather than appending, and the structured finding register has not been maintained since v7, so a real predecessor finding has no record anywhere in the subject
evidence: The slot was replaced, not extended. In predecessor v10, honestyRepairsFromV9 held exactly one entry recording the repair of Codex HAE9-CX-01: 'classPredicateDomain.rule now applies only to conditionals whose discriminator is consentRecords[].actionClass. policyProvenance.nullWhen is declared under consentCarrierPredicateDomain...'. In v11 that same index holds the CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 repair instead, and honestyRepairsFromV9 still has length 1.
The displaced finding survives nowhere in the subject. A raw scan of the 79689-byte v11 JSON returns zero occurrences of the string HAE9-CX-01.

Both findings belong to the same slot under the artifact's own convention. HAE9-CX-01 and CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 were both raised against v9, so honestyRepairsFromV9 should carry two entries. v11 demonstrates it understands the one-key-per-generation convention by correctly creating a new honestyRepairsFromV10 for the v10-generation finding.

The structured register stopped being maintained three rounds ago. predecessorVerdictFindings has top-level keys ['prior','v6','v7'] only, recording HAE5-CX-01, HAE6-CX-01 and HAE7-CX-01 each with a disposition. There is no v8, v9 or v10 entry, so neither the v8 dual ACCEPT, nor either v9 verdict, nor the v10 Codex REJECT is recorded in the register that exists for exactly that purpose.

The authorityClaim then presents an incomplete outstanding-findings picture, stating only 'It repairs Codex HAE10-CX-01 and Claude CLAUDE-HEA9-S1', with no mention that a Codex finding against v9 existed and was repaired a generation earlier.

The substantive repair of HAE9-CX-01 is intact in the contract body, which bounds the severity: classPredicateDomain.rule still reads 'Every when / nullWhen / requiredWhen predicate whose discriminator is consentRecords[].actionClass ... This rule does not quantify over consentCarrier-domain predicates', and consentCarrierPredicateDomain is present. The loss is of the record, not of the fix.
shouldFix.impact: A reviewer or coordinator reading v11 alone cannot determine that Codex raised HAE9-CX-01, that it was repaired in v10, or that its repair is what classPredicateDomain.rule's narrowing now encodes. Because this lineage gates on dual independent verdicts and successors are reviewed against the accumulated finding set, an artifact that silently drops a predecessor finding removes the very evidence a later reviewer needs to check whether that repair was preserved or quietly regressed. The frozen Codex v9 verdict is still pinned in recordedInputs and so remains recoverable off-artifact, which is why this is not graded a blocker.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restore the HAE9-CX-01 entry to honestyRepairsFromV9 and carry CLAUDE-HEA9-S1 as a second entry in that array, so the v9 generation's two findings are both recorded. Extend predecessorVerdictFindings with v8, v9 and v10 rounds in the shape already used for v6 and v7, each naming the verdict, the pinned digest, and per-finding dispositions. State the rule the platform lineage uses in terms: replacing a repair record is not a withdrawal of the finding it records.

advisories.title: FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS exercises no CA-3 row and only one accept case
advisories.observation: The new fixture's parentRecords cover CA-1, CA-1-HOST-HEAD, CA-2, CA-4 and CA-4-HOST but never CA-3, which is the class with the largest subtype domain, four values including the deferred KEYCHAIN. There is a single accept-shape row, CA-1 with SPAWN; no accept case exists for CA-3, for CA-4 or CA-4-HOST with a PATH-* subtype, or for CA-1-HOST-HEAD on the record side.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The binding itself is stated normatively and completely at three places: the record perClassMap over all four record literals, the serialized per-class lists over CA-1 to CA-4, and the extended unmatchedSerializedClass which enumerates CA-3's domain explicitly. The fixture's job is to make the rule testable and it does reject the cross-class case the finding was about. Coverage breadth is a fixture-population concern.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. Add a CA-3 accept row, a CA-3 cross-class refuse row, and a PATH-* accept row so every class has both polarities.

advisories.title: doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.actionSubtype still states its requiredness over a mixed vocabulary
advisories.observation: The entry reads 'consentRecords[].scope.actionSubtype. Required for CA-1, CA-3, CA-4-HOST. Null only for CA-2. Unpopulated subtype on CA-1/CA-3/CA-4 is UNCLASSIFIED and DENIED, matching nullWhen and FC-C5.' The first requiredness clause mixes serialized CA-1 and CA-3 with the record literal CA-4-HOST, and the next sentence restates the same condition in the fully serialized form CA-1/CA-3/CA-4. v11 corrected the analogous mixing in closedMembers[3].nullWhen but left this one.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: doctorV4FieldMapping is the designated home for translation, so both vocabularies legitimately appear there, and the immediately following sentence supplies the unambiguous serialized form. No predicate elsewhere depends on this sentence's phrasing.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. Make the first clause read CA-1-HOST-HEAD, CA-3, CA-4-HOST if it describes record classes, or CA-1, CA-3, CA-4 if it describes the serialized destination.

measurements.hae10Cx01Detail: Judged against Codex's frozen requiredRepair text rather than the dispatch summary. Clause one, register both predicates: consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo now lists both members[policyProvenance].nullWhen and .requiredWhen, and the member additionally carries nullWhenDomain and requiredWhenDomain, satisfying both of Codex's alternatives. Clause two, replace closedValuesWhenPresent: true: the boolean is gone and a closed source-identity object with extrasRejected, a stated digest encoding and string bounds takes its place. Clause three, exercise the typed value: FC-CARRIER-SHAPE now supplies a concrete four-member provenance object, a malformed single-member object, a null under pre-existing-policy, and a non-object string, each with an expected result. The finding is answered. The type declaration that the chosen option required was not updated, which is CLAUDE-HEA11-S1.
